target: UTM-bundled QEMU, AArch64 PCI, one vCPU, disposable writable RedSea VirtIO fixture
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/tosmisc-cycle-redsea-current-qemu.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-raw-redsea-geometry cycle
result: pass: recursive enumeration omitted a directory back-edge, and stock DiskCheck returned cleanly
verified: The probe ran against a private copy-on-write disk with a 128-sector RedSea fixture containing a valid root and SUB directory.
SUB contains a LOOP directory entry that points back to the root directory.
FilesFind('D:/SUB', FUF_JUST_DIRS | FUF_SINGLE) returns SUB, while FilesFind('D:/SUB/LOOP', FUF_JUST_DIRS | FUF_SINGLE) returns no entry.
DiskCheck('D', FALSE, FALSE) returns zero; the probe returns 42 and zstatus reports failed=0.
limits: This covers one read-only ancestor back-edge; directory repair, malformed metadata repair, FAT32, live UTM UI, and physical Raspberry Pi behavior remain unverified.
